info.title: Nex Core host-local API
info.description: Development host-local HTTPS API v1, independent of Controller sessions and outages. Narrow appliance deployment and owned local power recovery; a local VM console WebSocket; no generic VM creation or network editor. Core outbound protocol and signed appliance format/protocol version 1 only. Deploy matching development components; no mixed-version upgrade window is promised.

servers.description: Selected Nex Core host; never the Controller API origin.

post.description: Authenticates only username root against the host operating-system password using PAM authentication and account checks, and validates browser origin. Use the root password set during Nex Core installation, or its current value after an OS password change. Locked or expired accounts/passwords and authentication-service failures fail closed, including the five-second helper timeout. Sets __Host-nex_local_session with Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/ and no Domain. Each login creates a new session; at most 64 active sessions per service. Sessions expire after 30 minutes without an authenticated mutation and eight hours absolutely; GET/HEAD polling does not renew them. Legacy unprefixed cookies are not accepted; sign in again after upgrade. The former separate local admin account and saved credential files are not accepted; there is no fallback. Upgrades require matching local service, PAM helper/configuration and web assets. Root password changes affect subsequent logins; existing sessions remain valid until logout, expiry or service restart. Controller admin credentials and Core protocol v1 are unchanged. Local process restart invalidates its in-memory sessions. Login admission permits at most five valid-length attempts per one-minute actual peer-IP window, two concurrent password checks per service, and 4096 tracked peers. Forwarded client-IP headers are ignored. Login returns 429 when rate/concurrency/table or 64-session capacity is exhausted; bounded retries must not create an unbounded loop.

400.description: HTTPS required, invalid JSON/input, password outside 1–1024 UTF-8 bytes or containing NUL; invalid password input is rejected before invoking the helper.

403.description: Origin must equal the request HTTPS origin; authenticated mutations also require the session CSRF token.

415.description: application/json required; request body limited to 32 KiB. Unknown fields and multiple JSON values are rejected with 400.

401.description: Authentication denied: wrong password, username other than root, locked or expired root account/password, or unavailable authentication helper. No local admin fallback.

429.description: Login admission permits at most five valid-length attempts per one-minute actual peer-IP window, two concurrent password checks per service, and 4096 tracked peers. Forwarded client-IP headers are ignored. Login returns 429 when rate/concurrency/table or 64-session capacity is exhausted; bounded retries must not create an unbounded loop. No Retry-After header is emitted because concurrency saturation has no fixed expiry.

post.description: Explicitly select the resident VM UUID. Only locally owned eligible appliances can be controlled; arbitrary guests and ambiguous ownership are refused. start, graceful shutdown and force-stop are supported. The client confirms the selected VM/action; no typed hostname is required and the legacy confirmation field is ignored. Persist a request_id before submission. Reusing the same ID/input observes the existing journal; interrupted or ambiguous effects are not automatically repeated. A 202 response is not proof of final power state: inspect the operation and fresh VM inventory. Controller outage neither stops guests nor permits takeover. Graceful shutdown returns stage shutdown_requested when the command is accepted; refresh VM inventory to establish actual shutdown. Power request journals are reconciled by resubmitting the same request; deployment polling routes do not expose power operations.

post.description: Persists one deployment intent before asynchronous work. Set a stable request_id, explicit configured local storage/bridge, resources, network_mode (static or dhcp), first Site and Controller password. Zero or omitted resource fields use 2 vCPUs, 4096 MiB and 32 GiB. Repeating identical normalized input returns the same operation; different input or a second deployment conflicts. The worker verifies the signed appliance, creates an independent disk and cloud-init seed, starts the original VM, verifies Controller TLS and completes enrollment/adoption. Poll the operation; guest boot is not completed handoff. Interrupted VM effects require observation and never recreate the appliance. DHCP waits up to five minutes at waiting_for_network for one usable IPv4 address from the guest agent on the exact owned VM/MAC; missing or ambiguous addresses produce needs_attention and can be retried. controller_url is absent until an address is found. The discovered IP is verified using the per-instance Controller certificate and hostname before handoff. DHCP requires matching rebuilt host and appliance components; omitted network_mode preserves static clients.

post.description: Explicitly retry the original persisted intent by its request ID without reposting the administrator password. Concurrent retries share the existing worker; a ready static operation remains unchanged, while DHCP rediscovery can refresh its address. VM effects reconcile the original journal and UUID instead of recreating or repeating an uncertain start. Handoff can resume after Controller connectivity returns. DHCP retry and service startup rediscover the original VM address and verify its saved certificate/hostname; ready DHCP startup does this before resuming the existing enrolled agent. A changed lease with an active agent returns needs_attention requiring a local-service restart. This retains VM/host identities and does not require the original administrator password. Leases are not monitored periodically. A 202 response only accepts the retry; poll the original operation until ready or needs_attention.

post.summary: Push an enrollment token to this host
post.description: Lets the Controller enroll this host over its existing local session instead of the manual nex-core-agent enroll step. controller_url must be a bare HTTPS origin (no userinfo, path, query or fragment); ca_pem must contain at least one certificate; token must be 1-256 bytes with no control characters; replace_host, when set, is an existing revoked host id being replaced and must be at most 128 characters. Enrollment attempts on this host are serialized; a retried request queues rather than racing the embedded agent's on-disk identity. Already enrolled with a different replace_host returns 409 with the current host_id and changes nothing. On success the embedded agent persists its new identity, starts reporting to the Controller, and the response host_id also appears from GET /api/local/v1/host. The Controller's rejection of the token (expired, already used, wrong site) surfaces as 502 and leaves this host unenrolled; retrying with a fresh token is safe. The token and ca_pem are never logged or echoed back.

get.summary: Open a local VM console WebSocket
get.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0. WebSocket upgrade (RFC 6455, binary frames carrying raw RFB/VNC bytes for noVNC) authenticated by the local root session cookie; the Origin header must equal this host's HTTPS origin. The selected VM must be running on this host's system libvirt with a local UNIX-socket VNC display; any other display type is refused. The service bridges the browser to that socket directly and never opens a network VNC listener. This works without Nex Controller and is intended for guest installation and recovery from the host itself.

101.description: WebSocket established; binary frames relay the VM display stream.

200.description: Not returned; the stream is the 101 response.

400.description: HTTPS required or missing WebSocket upgrade headers.

401.description: Missing or expired local administrator session.

403.description: Origin must equal the request HTTPS origin.

409.description: VM is not running, not found, or has no local VNC socket display.

503.description: The VM console socket refused the connection.

get.description: Checks the configured package repo updates.json for nex-core-local. Repo failures surface in error with HTTP 200. Root local session required.

post.description: Downloads the nex-core-local deb from the configured repo, runs dpkg -i as root, then schedules systemctl restart via systemd-run --no-block. Returns 202 scheduled on success. CSRF and same-origin required.

LocalSession.name: __Host-nex_local_session
LocalSession.description: Administrator session cookie __Host-nex_local_session, Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict, Path=/ with no Domain. Expires after 30 minutes without an authenticated mutation or eight hours absolutely. GET/HEAD polling does not extend idle lifetime; mutations also require matching Origin and X-CSRF-Token. At most 64 active sessions per service. Legacy unprefixed cookies are refused; sign in again after upgrading.

x-session-policy.idle_refresh: authenticated mutations after Origin/CSRF validation; GET and HEAD never extend it

status.description: Inspect status and error independently of progress. A running guest alone does not prove Controller handoff. needs_attention retains original identity and requires reconciliation. recovery_prepared is a manual CLI result only; it confirms an empty replacement awaiting explicit archive restore, not recovered Controller identity.

progress.description: Coarse workflow stage percentage, not measured bytes or estimated remaining time. ready at 100 indicates completed deployment handoff and seed cleanup. completed power operations acknowledge command completion; shutdown_requested does not prove the guest stopped.

controller_url.description: Controller HTTPS address when known. DHCP discovers an owned guest IPv4 address before publishing it; absence while waiting_for_network is expected. ready still requires verified handoff.

controller_cert_sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 fingerprint of the Controller leaf certificate DER. Verify this identity before trusting the new Controller browser certificate.

power_allowed.description: Local ownership eligibility; operations revalidate ownership and current observation before execution.

ready.description: Current host capacity, signed manifest and compatibility checks passed. This does not establish full image integrity or format safety; deployment verifies those before effects.

image_verification.description: Explains the verification boundary: preflight checks the signed manifest and compatibility metadata; full image SHA-256 and qcow2 safety checks run during deployment. Read blockers to determine whether manifest validation succeeded.

request_id.description: Persist before submitting. Stable identifier; replay must use identical normalized settings including original password.

address_cidr.description: Static usable unicast IPv4 address with /8–/30 prefix; subnet and broadcast addresses are refused. Required for static mode; omitted in DHCP mode.

gateway.description: Another usable IPv4 address in the selected subnet, excluding subnet and broadcast addresses. Required for static mode; omitted in DHCP mode.

dns.description: One to three unicast IPv4 DNS server addresses. Required for static mode; omitted in DHCP mode.

admin_password.description: Initial Controller administrator secret: nonempty valid UTF-8, at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes, no CR, LF or NUL. No minimum length or complexity rule. Never included in operation responses. Retained privately only until handoff and seed cleanup complete.

site_name.description: Required nonblank name, maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes.

bridge.description: Explicitly select the configured existing management bridge. Deployment does not create or edit host networks.

storage_dir.description: Explicitly select the configured local storage directory returned by host preflight; this is not a pool/shared storage registration.

network_mode.description: Omitted or empty uses static for compatibility. The deployment UI defaults to DHCP. DHCP obtains IPv4 addressing, gateway and DNS from the selected bridge network. DHCP refuses nonempty static address, gateway or DNS fields.

phase.description: idle, downloading, installing, restarting, done, or failed when an apply is tracked.

progress.description: Percent complete for the current apply when known.

error.description: Non-fatal repo or apply problem; installed_version remains valid for check.

nex-core-local -prepare-recovery-file.description: Root-only manual replacement preparation, not an HTTP operation or running listener. Requires stopped local service and a clean replacement host without outbound agent identity or normal deployments. Uses the selected signed appliance and existing local storage/bridge. Does not bootstrap a Site, enroll a host or adopt the VM. Repeated identical normalized file contents reconcile the persisted request and original VM UUID; changed contents fail. TLS-verified readiness and seed removal precede recovery_prepared.

inputFile.validation: One JSON object in a regular file; unknown fields rejected.

output.format: One JSON object on stdout after successful completion.

nex-core-local -prepare-recovery-file.failure: Nonzero exit and error on stderr. Retain original request and journal; inspect uncertain VM effects before retry. No automatic restore, takeover or enrollment.
nex-core-local -prepare-recovery-file.compatibility: Same signed appliance format/protocol v1 and architecture amd64 as ordinary deployment. Restore requires matching source SHA-256 via the separate manual recovery command.
